behavior: The backend gives each profile one Privy wallet through internal/privy
acceptance: internal/privy returns a profile's user-owned EVM wallet: it creates one with external_id = profile id or returns the existing one found by external_id and owner, never a second; two concurrent creates end with one wallet; another user never gets it; a failed create doesn't block later ones; the address comes back lowercase

A fake Privy API (httptest, checking auth headers and request bodies, replaying cached errors per idempotency key) covers create, lookup, the create race, a failed create and another user; an opt-in test (build tag privylive) creates a user and asks for its profile wallet twice against the Privy test app
notes: 2026-10-09 review fail by reviewer: FAIL. Defect: apps/backend/internal/privy/privy.go:43 sends a fixed privy-idempotency-key per profile. Privy docs (docs.privy.io/api-reference/idempotency-keys) say wallet create caches 4xx AND 5xx responses for the key's 24h lifetime and replays them; a new key is needed to retry. So one transient 5xx (or a 4xx such as a not-yet-visible user) during signup (R-32) blocks that profile's wallet for 24h: every retry, including the SDK's own 2 retries, replays the cached error. The key adds no safety: external_id is documented 'Unique per app. No two wallets in the same app can share an external_id' (docs.privy.io/wallets/wallets/external-ids), and the lookup-after-failed-create already covers the race. Fix: drop the idempotency key (line 43), update accept 1 and docs/backend/architecture.md:75, and add a fake case where the first create returns 500 and the next call succeeds (fake should replay cached errors per idempotency key, or assert no key is sent). Non-blocking: (1) privy.go:56 lists by external_id only; add UserID: privyUserID so a wallet owned by another Privy user is never returned (a caller passing a wrong user then fails closed via the create conflict instead of getting someone else's wallet). (2) List hides archived wallets by default (include_archived=false), so an archived profile wallet makes ProfileWallet fail with the create error; fine while nothing archives. (3) privy_test.go:150 only proves a failed lookup is reported, not 'create fails and lookup finds nothing returns the create error'. (4) The fake answers duplicate external_id with 409 (privy_test.go:65), which the SDK retries twice with backoff (tests take 1.3-1.5s); real Privy's duplicate code is undocumented; outcome is the same since any create error falls back to lookup. (5) SDK DefaultClientOptions reads PRIVY_APP_ID/SECRET/API_BASE_URL/API_CUSTOM_HEADERS from env; explicit options override the first three, CUSTOM_HEADERS would still apply (outside internal/config). OK: UUID profile ids are valid external_ids (36 chars, [0-9a-f-]); fallback cannot mask auth errors (lookup fails the same way) and can only return the wallet created for this external_id; SDK logging defaults to LogLevelNone, no header/body logs; timeouts come from ctx plus 10m response-header timeout; go.mod only adds lines, golang.org/x/crypto stays v0.55.0 (MVS picks max over SDK's v0.41.0), go mod tidy -diff clean, go mod verify ok; vet with e2e,privylive tags fine; no interface added, API URL injected, fits rules.md. Ran: pnpm --filter @forwend/backend test (all ok, privy 3.99s); live test -tags privylive PASS 3.77s.

2026-10-09 review pass by reviewer: PASS on re-review of ea13b9b. Blocking finding fixed: privy.go no longer sends an idempotency key on wallet create, so a cached Privy error can no longer block a profile's wallet for 24h; duplicates are prevented by external_id (unique per app per Privy docs) plus the lookup after a failed create. Note 1 fixed: find() filters by ExternalID and UserID, so a wrong user gets an error (create conflicts, filtered lookup finds nothing), never another user's wallet. Fake now replays cached errors per idempotency key, fails N creates with 500, filters by user_id; TestProfileWalletRecoversFromAFailedCreate would fail with the old fixed key (the replayed 500), TestProfileWalletBelongsToItsUser would fail without the owner filter. Accept lines and docs/backend/architecture.md updated. Ran: pnpm --filter @forwend/backend test (all ok, privy 6.5s); go test -race -count=5 ./internal/privy/ ok (no flakes). Live privylive test not re-run by this reviewer (one run allowed, used on the first review; it passed then); the coordinator reports it passes with the owner filter. Nits, not blocking: privy_test.go:27,69 the fake still records keys but no test reads them; docs/backend/architecture.md:78 leaves a short line before 'for these wallets'; still open from the first review: archived wallets are hidden by List (include_archived=false), and PRIVY_API_CUSTOM_HEADERS from env is applied by the SDK.
